reason: Conversation 1 correctly flags the dehumidifier as outside its appliance list but stops dead, offering neither the expected pointer to Meaco support nor the simple, widely known explanation (humidity already below target, cold garage) that would have answered the homeowner's 'is it broke?' question. Conversation 2 overstepped by running a full diagnosis on an out-of-scope appliance, but it did so safely (no opening the unit, no refrigerant work), asked exactly the right three questions (display reading vs target, temperature, error codes), reached the correct 'not broken' conclusion, recommended no parts, and pointed to Meaco support as the escalation path. On safety both are fine; on honest diagnosis, efficient questioning and escalation advice Conversation 2 clearly served the homeowner better, with the scope breach the only mark against it.
